comparator.name: Business and Consumer Studies (Bedrijfs- en Consumentenwetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Current WUR programme page and published cohort-2025 curriculum, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The official three-year programme totals 180 EC. Year 1 is a 60-EC common foundation in business, marketing, sociology, law, mathematics, statistics, research and food quality. From year 2 students choose Business or Consumer. The normalized target names neither specialisation, so Business is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break because it appears first in the official programme and legend. The Business route contains 60 EC in year 2, including two genuine restricted choices and the programme-wide professionalisation trajectory, followed in year 3 by 24 EC of named Business study, a 12-EC thesis and 24 EC genuine free choice. Zero-credit General Safety is acknowledged but omitted from the credit-bearing component list.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specialisation. The official curriculum presents Business and Consumer as parallel routes without designating a general route. Business appears first, so it is selected independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Business strategy, markets & supply chains
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible business-specialisation programme combining management, strategy, economics, accounting, marketing, entrepreneurship, organisational behaviour, supply-chain thinking, data, research and responsible decision-making.
alternatives.labelReason: Management, strategy, economics, accounting, marketing, entrepreneurship, organisational behaviour and market research form the programme spine, matching the neutrally selected Business specialisation.
progression: Business, economics, programming and professional foundations precede strategy, marketing, management, organisational behaviour, market research, econometrics and advanced business decisions. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Consumer behaviour, marketing & product insight
alternatives.concept: Combines consumer psychology, behavioural economics, marketing, market research, product design, negotiation, business, data and communication to understand choices and create products and messages people value.
alternatives.labelReason: Consumer engagement, behavioural economics, market research, product design, psychology, negotiation and data analysis form a visible consumer-insight and marketing spine.
progression: Business, economics, research and data foundations precede consumer marketing, behavioural economics, product design, negotiation and market research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest Business-specialisation programme, this route replaces supply-chain, organisational and several strategy components with consumer product design, behavioural economics, consumer marketing, negotiation and product insight. Five courses differ in each programme, clearing the 30-EC floor.

alternatives.label: Sustainable & circular business transformation
alternatives.concept: Combines economics, business, international governance, strategy and leadership with sustainability science, life-cycle analysis, circular resource systems, public policy and ethical reasoning to transform firms and value chains responsibly.
alternatives.labelReason: Business and economics are integrated with life-cycle analysis, climate, circular-resource recovery, governance and sustainability policy across the full programme.
progression: Business, economics, ethics, sociology and sustainability foundations precede international governance, circular resource systems, leadership, public economics and responsible transformation. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; nine 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs from both prior programmes by replacing consumer-product, marketing and data-heavy study with sustainability science, life-cycle analysis, climate, circular resource recovery, environmental governance, public economics and political or ethical analysis. It differs by more than 30 EC from each.

selection.assessment: The first programme is the closest feasible response to the neutrally selected Business specialisation. Consumer insight and sustainable/circular transformation are independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions. Pairwise overlaps are 19, 13 and 10 courses respectively, so all alternatives clear the 30-EC distinctness floor. A further business-intelligence route remains evidenced but is not attempted after reaching the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR integrates business and consumer science around food and value chains, offers named Business and Consumer specialisations, and requires a 12-EC thesis. UCR can build strong business, consumer, data and sustainability pathways, but does not reproduce WUR’s exact food-quality, sensory-science, decision-science or supply-chain sequence. The alternatives are academically defensible related programmes rather than structural equivalence.
